overview: This little 4-legged square switch with a distinctive audible/tactile click is probably the single most-used input component in hobby electronics — soldered directly onto breadboards and PCBs everywhere from reset buttons to game controllers. Its four legs are actually only two electrical connections: each side's two legs are permanently joined together (purely for mechanical stability when soldered), so it doesn't matter which of a pair you use, but the two pairs must go to different signal nets or the switch will read as permanently closed.
simpleSummary: The small clicky button soldered onto nearly every circuit board and breadboard project.

specifications.ratedVoltage: Typically rated for low-voltage logic circuits (12V/50mA or similar)
specifications.footprint: Standard 6mm square THT package fits standard breadboard hole spacing

pinMap.name: Pin 1/2 (Side A)
pinMap.function: Both legs on one side of the switch — internally joined, electrically identical to each other.
pinMap.gotcha: All four legs look identical, but only diagonal pairs (or the two on each 'side') are internally bridged — check orientation, since bridging the wrong pair can make the switch appear stuck closed.

pinMap.name: Pin 3/4 (Side B)
pinMap.function: Both legs on the other side of the switch — internally joined, connects to Side A when pressed.
pinMap.gotcha: Needs a pull-up or pull-down resistor (or the microcontroller's internal pull-up) so the input reads a defined level when not pressed, rather than floating.

useCases.title: Reset/mode button
useCases.scenario: A simple momentary input for resetting state or cycling through modes.

useCases.title: Game controller buttons
useCases.scenario: Multiple tactile switches wired as action buttons for a DIY game controller.

useCases.title: Keypad matrix input
useCases.scenario: Arranged in a grid with diode isolation to build a custom button matrix with fewer pins than one-per-button.

oftenConfusedWith: Panel-mount push button (larger, mounted through an enclosure wall)
oftenUpgradedTo: Membrane keypad for many inputs without dozens of individual switches
